TEDU Without Barriers Unit Directive 
 
SECTION ONE  
Aim, Scope, Basis and Definitions 
ARTICLE 1 – (1) The aim of this directive is to take the necessary measures to facilitate the 
lives of disabled students enrolled at TED University as well as disabled academic and 
administrative staff members working at the university; to regulate the working procedures and 
principles of the TEDU Without Barriers Unit established to ensure equality in academic, 
professional, social and cultural environments. 
ARTICLE 2 – (1) This directive has been prepared based on the Law No. 5378 on Persons 
with Disabilities published in the Official Gazette dated 07.07.2005 and numbered 25868 and 
the Regulation on Disability Counseling and Coordination in Higher Education Institutions 
published in the Official Gazette.

the Regulation on Disability Counseling and Coordination in Higher Education Institutions 
published in the Official Gazette. 
ARTICLE 3 – (1) Definitions of certain terms used in this document are as follows:  
a) Students/Staff with Disabilities: Students or staff who have difficulties in adapting to 
social life and meeting their daily needs due to the loss of physical, mental, spiritual, 
emotional and social abilities to various degrees due to any reason, whether congenital 
or acquired, and who need protection, care, rehabilitation, counseling and support 
services, 
b) TEDU without Barriers Unit: The unit established in accordance with the Higher 
Education Institutions Disability Consultation and Coordination Regulation published 
in the Official Gazette, 
c) Disabled Student Representative: A student who represents disabled students at the 
University and has a disability, 
ç) Student Council Representative: The student who represents the disabled students at

University and has a disability, 
ç) Student Council Representative: The student who represents the disabled students at 
the university and takes an active role in the student council, 
d) Rector: TED University Rector,  
e) University: TED University,

registration in coordination with the Registrar's Office, 
b) To conduct a comprehensive needs analysis at the beginning of each academic year with 
the opinions of students and staff with disabilities and to ensure that the campus,

SECTION THREE 
Principles for Education and Training Practices 
Responsibilities of Instructors 
ARTICLE 6 – (1) Instructors are responsible for acting in accordance with the legal regulations 
determined for disabled students and carrying out the necessary legal practices according to the 
disability status of the students.

(3) It is the responsibility of the instructors to carry out the education and training process by 
considering the condition of students with disabilities.  
(4) In order to provide educational comfort to students with disabilities, instructors must contact 
the TEDU without Barriers Unit for the provision of materials and devices that students 
need during the course. 
(5) Instructors must contact the TEDU without Barriers Unit in case of problems with students' 
access to the educational environment. 
(6) Instructors refer students with special needs to the TEDU without Barriers Unit when they 
realize that they have special needs during the education process. 
(7) Instructors must prepare the course content taking into account the needs of different 
disability groups.

Responsibilities of Students with Disabilities 
ARTICLE 7 – (1) Students with disabilities must contact the TEDU without Barriers Unit in 
order to access academic, social and cultural support more easily. 
(2) At the beginning of each semester, it is the responsibility of the students to communicate 
with the instructors of the courses they are enrolled in and to inform the instructors about 
their specific situation and needs. 
(3) Students with disabilities contact the TEDU without Barriers Unit for the support they need 
during the course preparation process. 
(4) Students with disabilities must keep their contact information up to date on TEDU Portal. 
(5) Students with disabilities must contact the TEDU without Barriers Unit in case of a change 
in their disability status.

SECTION FOUR 
Principles for the Conduct of Examinations 
ARTICLE 8 – (1) Exam venues are to be organized taking into account the accessibility of 
disabled students.   
(2) If necessary, the instructor may change the exam method used in the course according to 
the student's disability by contacting the TEDU without Barriers Unit.

(5) If needed, a reader and a marker/writer who is familiar with the terminology of the course

(6) If needed, students with disabilities are allowed to take exams with medication or medical

(7) If needed, students with disabilities are allowed to use the restroom during the exam under 
the supervision of the proctor. 
 
SECTION FIVE 
Principles for the Implementation of Social-Cultural Activities 
ARTICLE 9 – (1) At the beginning of each academic year, orientation activities are to be 
carried out by the Student Activities Office in cooperation with TEDU without Barriers Unit in 
order to accelerate the adaptation of newly enrolled disabled students to the academic, social 
and cultural environment of the University.

order to accelerate the adaptation of newly enrolled disabled students to the academic, social 
and cultural environment of the University. 
(2) The accessibility of social-cultural activities organized by the academic and administrative

Article 5 - (1) The Commission consists of members determined by the Senate from the 
faculty/institute and relevant academic and administrative units, along with a student 
representative, under the chairmanship of the Rector. The term of office for members is two 
years, and a member whose term has expired may be reappointed. The term of office for the 
student representative is one year, and they are selected at the beginning of each academic year 
and reported to the commission. 
(2) The chairmanship of the Commission is held by the Rector, and in the absence of the Rector, 
it is carried out by the Vice Rector appointed by the Rector.  
(3) If a member fails to attend three consecutive commission meetings within a calendar year

it is carried out by the Vice Rector appointed by the Rector.  
(3) If a member fails to attend three consecutive commission meetings within a calendar year 
without an excuse, their membership will be terminated, and a new member will be appointed 
in their place. If a membership becomes vacant for any reason, an appointment will be made in 
the same manner.

the commission, will be announced on the university's website.

1. Objective and Scope 
The purpose of this guideline is to ensure that all exams administered at TED University (midterm exams, 
final exams, make-up exams, resit exams, supplementary exams, etc.) are conducted in a fair, secure, and 
orderly manner by establishing the rules that students must follow. 
2. Before the Exam Begins 
(1) Unless stated otherwise, students must arrive at the exam hall at least 10 minutes prior to the scheduled 
start time. 
(2) For identity verification purposes, each student must have their TEDU student ID card or official photo 
ID (Turkish ID card, passport, driver's license, photo student ID, etc.) with them. The instructor of the 
relevant course will decide whether a student who cannot present a valid ID will be allowed to take the

relevant course will decide whether a student who cannot present a valid ID will be allowed to take the 
exam, and the situation will be recorded in a report. 
(3) Students must bring only the necessary stationery (pencil, eraser, etc.) and materials specified in 
advance by the instructor for the exam. 
(4) Except for materials deemed necessary by the instructor of the relevant course, students are not allowed 
to bring any resources (books, notebooks, lecture notes, etc.) and all electronic devices (cell phones, 
pagers, walkie-talkies, wired and wireless headphones, communication devices such as radios, handheld 
computers and multi-function calculators, cameras or glasses with headphone functionality, watches with 
functions other than analog timekeeping) must be turned off and handed over to the proctor. Using any 
open mode, including airplane mode, is strictly prohibited. If electronic devices are detected on students 
during the exam, disciplinary action will be initiated.

open mode, including airplane mode, is strictly prohibited. If electronic devices are detected on students 
during the exam, disciplinary action will be initiated. 
(5) Students are obliged to follow the seating regulation as instructed by the proctor. The proctor may 
change the seat of a student before or during the exam. The exam of a student who fails to obey seating 
instructions will be cancelled, the situation will be recorded in a report, and the student will be dismissed 
from the exam hall. 
(6) In cases when the exam starts later than announced due to an unexpected reason, exam proctor is to 
inform everyone. Unless a cancellation or postponement is announced, students shall stay at the exam hall. 
3. During the Exam 
(1) Students are required to comply with the rules specified by the course instructor regarding the start and 
end times of the exam and the earliest time they can leave the exam hall after the exam has started.

end times of the exam and the earliest time they can leave the exam hall after the exam has started. 
(2) Students must wait for the proctor's instructions to begin the exam after the exam sheets have been 
handed out.

SECTION ONE 
Aim, Scope and Definitions 
Aim and Scope 
ARTICLE 1 – (1) The aim of this document is to set out the procedures and principles regarding the 
processes of Higher Nationals in Business certificate programs offered to undergraduate students at TED 
University. 
Definitions and Abbreviations 
ARTICLE 2 – (1) Definitions of certain terms used in this document are as follows: 
a) FAB: FEAS Faculty Administrative Board, 
b) GPA: Student's Program Grade Point Average, 
c) HN Programs: Higher Nationals Certificate (HNC) and Higher Nationals Diploma (HND)

b) GPA: Student's Program Grade Point Average, 
c) HN Programs: Higher Nationals Certificate (HNC) and Higher Nationals Diploma (HND) 
certificate programs offered by TED University in accordance with the IP license agreement 
with Pearson, 
d) HN Program Advisor: An advisor is assigned to each student in the HN Program. The duty of the 
advisor is to help the student organize the HN education-training program, to organize the 
course adjustment at the end of each semester and to provide guidance within the framework of 
the program.

Administration,

to HN programs are decided by the FAB.   
(3) The HN program is a certificate program independent from the undergraduate program in which the 
student is enrolled.

ARTICLE 6 – (1) Students who have the right to graduate from the undergraduate program and

FAB.   
 (2) Students who have graduated/dismissed from the undergraduate program and have not yet 
completed the HN Program may attend, provided that they do not exceed the total HN program duration

      TED University 
Academic Integrity Statement for Students 
 
 
I.       
Aim 
 
TED University carries the mission of fostering individuals that are creative, critical-
minded, responsible, life-long learners; respectful of ethical values and other people’s rights, 
who adopt honesty and solidarity as a principle, and aiming at contributing to the world of 
science at universal level and pursuing excellence in research. 
 
To this end, this statement aims to clarify the actions considered as academic dishonesty 
within the framework of TED University Code of Ethics; to secure the proper use of 
resources, information and ideas; to establish the concept of academic ethics, and to 
delineate the procedures to be followed in case of violations against the principles of 
academic integrity.

taken by faculty members who have completed their 6th year at the University and the Research Leave 
for those young scholars with high research capacity at the beginning of their careers. The following 
general rules apply to both of these leaves:

individuals.

ERASMUS+ PROGRAMME and STUDY MOBILITY 
The Erasmus+ Programme is a grant programme offered by the European Union to support education, 
youth, and sports. The programme provides funding for education, training, internships, professional 
development, non-formal learning-based youth activities, and cooperation between institutions abroad. 
It comprises three main actions and two special actions, with the most common being the Learning 
Mobility of Individuals. Students can benefit from this programme through mobility projects, which 
support both education and internship periods, under the sub-activity area of Learning Mobility of 
Individuals. 
The Erasmus+ Programme Student Mobility for Studies is designed to support full-time degree students 
at the Associate, Bachelor's, Master's, and Doctorate levels in universities that hold the Erasmus Charter

at the Associate, Bachelor's, Master's, and Doctorate levels in universities that hold the Erasmus Charter 
for Higher Education (ECHE) in Turkey. Students are allowed to become exchange students and study 
for 12 months. Those who are selected and placed as the main candidates for this activity are entitled 
to receive a monthly Erasmus+ support grant for all or part of their mobility period. Additionally, the 
students do not pay tuition fees at the host university. The European Credit Transfer System (ECTS) is 
used to recognize the time spent by the students in the host country and the courses they take in their 
home university. 
Study mobility is carried out based on inter-institutional agreements. The mobility activity is limited to 
those students enrolled in formal education who carry out a part of their education in a higher education 
institution abroad that is a partner with an inter-institutional agreement. The student’s department and

institution abroad that is a partner with an inter-institutional agreement. The student’s department and 
the receiving institution must have an Inter-Institutional Agreement in place to study there with 
Erasmus+. 
Students can visit the Turkish National Agency website to get detailed information about the Erasmus+ 
Programme.

GREEN TRAVEL SUPPORT (TOP-UP FOR GREEN TRAVELLING) 
If students choose to travel in an environmentally friendly way, they may qualify for a one-time additional 
grant of 50 Euros and an individual support grant of up to 4 days for travel days. 
Green travel is defined as a journey that uses low-carbon emission public transportation, such as buses, 
trains, and shared cars. To be eligible for green travel support, students must use green travel for both 
their departure and return trips, and more than half of the entire trip must be made using these vehicles.

Objective, Scope, Basis and Definitions 
Objective 
ARTICLE 1– (1) This Directive has been issued to determine the quotas, the selection criteria, 
employment, weekly working hours and other provisions of undergraduate and graduate students to be 
employed part-time at TED University for the following purposes: 
a) To help students develop their theoretical, practical and professional skills by working in line with 
their interests and abilities; to contribute to their training as productive individuals who have acquired 
work discipline, 
b) To enable students to focus on more specialized areas of interest, and thus to take the first steps of

work discipline, 
b) To enable students to focus on more specialized areas of interest, and thus to take the first steps of 
specialization during undergraduate education and to continue it in graduate education,  
c) To contribute to the personal development of students,  
d) To support the development of their researcher aspects by enabling them to take part in research 
projects carried out by the relevant Department or Research Center, 
e) To increase the tendency of promising students to pursue an academic career in universities after 
graduation.

administrative units that will employ part-time students and students who will work part-time.

SECTION TWO 
Application and Admission Processes for Part-Time Students  
Requirements for Students to be Employed Part-Time 
ARTICLE 5- (1) Students who meet the following conditions may be employed as Part-Time Students at 
the University; 
a) Being a registered student at TED University, 
b) Not to be a graduate student without thesis, special student, student on leave of absence and 
international student, 
c) To be studying within the normal education period, 
d) Not to have received any disciplinary penalty, 
e) Not having been terminated due to breach of contract between the University and the student who 
was employed part-time in the previous semesters, 
f) To have the competencies required for the job to be employed,

was employed part-time in the previous semesters, 
f) To have the competencies required for the job to be employed, 
g) To have a GPA of 2.00/4.00 and above at the undergraduate level and 3.00/4.00 and above at the 
graduate level, 
h) Not having an income at the minimum wage level, except for orphan's pension and alimony, 
i) Not being abroad within the scope of ERASMUS+ mobility program. 
Determination of Quotas for Part-Time Students 
ARTICLE 6- (1) On the announced date, the units send the quota of students they want to employ on a 
part-time basis to the SCA, indicating the nature of the work they will employ students for.  
(2) The quotas for part-time students are determined by the SCA in line with the requests of the units during 
the fiscal year and submitted to the Rector for approval.

ERASMUS+ PROGRAMME & TRAINEESHIP MOBILITY 
Erasmus+ (2021–2027) is the European Union's funding programme for education, youth, and sports. 
It supports learning opportunities abroad, including studies, traineeships, professional development, 
non-formal youth activities, and cooperation between organisations.  
Under Key Action 1: Mobility of Individuals, Erasmus+ offers higher education students the opportunity 
to study, train, and gain professional experience in Europe. The programme is managed by the 
European Commission and implemented in Turkey by the Turkish National Agency. 
Erasmus+ Traineeship Mobility enables students enrolled in a higher education institution to undertake 
a traineeship (internship) abroad at a business, research institute, laboratory, or other organisation 
relevant to their academic field of study. Taking courses at a higher education institution is not

relevant to their academic field of study. Taking courses at a higher education institution is not 
considered a traineeship. To be considered valid, a traineeship must involve practical work experience 
with an economic value in the relevant sector, rather than being purely academic. The traineeship is not 
required to be a mandatory part of the student's degree programme. However, the sector in which the 
traineeship takes place must be relevant to the student's current programme of study. 
The duration of the mobility period can be between 2 and 12 months, applicable to each level of study. 
The traineeship can be undertaken at any point during each academic year, including within 12 months 
of graduation for students in their final year of study. For post-graduation traineeships, the application 
must be made before the student graduates (while still enrolled as an undergraduate, graduate, or

must be made before the student graduates (while still enrolled as an undergraduate, graduate, or 
postgraduate student). Students who have already graduated are not eligible to apply. The post-
graduation traineeship must be completed within 12 months of the graduation date. 
In terms of workload, participants are generally expected to work full-time, based on their receiving 
organisation's working hours.

SocialEASE TRAINEESHIP CONSORTIUM 
The SocialEASE Consortium Project is an EU-funded mobility project, coordinated by TED University, 
that aims to encourage students in Turkey to explore career paths with a social impact perspective by 
experiencing and learning about the field of social entrepreneurship.

that aims to encourage students in Turkey to explore career paths with a social impact perspective by 
experiencing and learning about the field of social entrepreneurship. 
Fundamentally, the project offers students the opportunity to participate in and gain experience from the 
work of social enterprises, creative industry organisations, and support organisations focused on social 
entrepreneurship in Europe, within the framework of Erasmus+ traineeship mobility. The ultimate goal 
is to contribute to the development of Turkey's social innovation and social entrepreneurship ecosystem 
by facilitating the transfer of knowledge gained from international experiences. 
Key components of SocialEASE include participants gaining hands-on experience as well as engaging 
in projects within this field. These activities are intended to equip participants with the practical 
knowledge and skills necessary to create impact in the fields of social entrepreneurship and creative 
industries.

knowledge and skills necessary to create impact in the fields of social entrepreneurship and creative 
industries. 
There are no faculty or departmental restrictions for traineeship activities carried out under this project. 
Traineeships in the fields of social entrepreneurship and creative industries, within the eligible 
traineeship placements specified in the Erasmus+ Programme Guide, are considered to fall within this 
scope. Therefore, students must obtain a letter of acceptance from an organisation operating in these 
fields, and the traineeship placement and programme must be suitable for the project's content. 
Students who would like to learn more about the project can visit our website.

Special Conditions for First-Year Students 
Based on the decision taken at the Internationalization Committee Meeting held on June 10, 2020, 
considering the limited places, it was decided that the following application principles would be taken 
into account for Erasmus+ Student and Traineeship Mobility starting from the 2020-2021 Academic 
Year: 
• 
First-year students can be selected for Erasmus+ mobility, but their number must not exceed 
50% of the total allocated places for their department. 
• 
If there are insufficient applications from upper-year students (sophomores and juniors), the 
remaining places will be allocated to first-year students.

Staff teaching mobility is the field of activity that allows a staff
member who is responsible for teaching at a higher
education institution (HEI) which holds ECHE
(Erasmus Charter for Higher Education) to teach
students at one of the partner universities in Programme
Countries (Member States of the European Union, North
Macedonia, Serbia, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway).
The objectives of the teaching mobility are:
To allow students who are not able to participate in a
mobility scheme to benefit from the knowledge and
expertise of academic staff from higher education
institutions in other European countries
To promote an exchange of expertise and experience on
pedagogical methods
To encourage higher education institutions to broaden and
enrich the range and content of courses they offer.
For staff to participate in teaching mobility, they must be
officially employed as teaching staff members on a full or

ERASMUS+ PROGRAMME & TRAINEESHIP MOBILITY 
Erasmus+ (2021–2027) is the European Union's funding programme for education, youth, and sports.

ERASMUS+ PROGRAMME & TRAINEESHIP MOBILITY 
Erasmus+ (2021–2027) is the European Union's funding programme for education, youth, and sports. 
It supports learning opportunities abroad, including studies, traineeships, professional development, 
non-formal youth activities, and cooperation between organisations.  
Under Key Action 1: Mobility of Individuals, Erasmus+ offers higher education students the opportunity 
to study, train, and gain professional experience in Europe. The programme is managed by the 
European Commission and implemented in Turkey by the Turkish National Agency. 
Erasmus+ Traineeship Mobility enables students enrolled in a higher education institution to undertake 
a traineeship (internship) abroad at a business, research institute, laboratory, or other organisation 
relevant to their academic field of study. Taking courses at a higher education institution is not

relevant to their academic field of study. Taking courses at a higher education institution is not 
considered a traineeship. To be considered valid, a traineeship must involve practical work experience 
with an economic value in the relevant sector, rather than being purely academic. The traineeship is not 
required to be a mandatory part of the student's degree programme. However, the sector in which the 
traineeship takes place must be relevant to the student's current programme of study. 
The duration of the mobility period can be between 2 and 12 months, applicable to each level of study. 
The traineeship can be undertaken at any point during each academic year, including within 12 months 
of graduation for students in their final year of study. For post-graduation traineeships, the application 
must be made before the student graduates (while still enrolled as an undergraduate, graduate, or

must be made before the student graduates (while still enrolled as an undergraduate, graduate, or 
postgraduate student). Students who have already graduated are not eligible to apply. The post-
graduation traineeship must be completed within 12 months of the graduation date. 
In terms of workload, participants are generally expected to work full-time, based on their receiving 
organisation's working hours.

PRINCIPLES OF APPLICATION, ADMISSION, AND REGISTRATION TO

Application, admission and registration procedures are implemented in accordance with the “Principles 
on the Admission of Foreign Students” by the Council of Higher Education, and with TED University 
“Regulation on Undergraduate Education.” 
Quotas, Admission and Evaluation 
1. International student quotas may not exceed 50% of the quotas of the programs given in the Student 
Selection and Placement Exam (ÖSYS) Guide on Higher Education Programs and Quotas of the 
preceding year. 
2. Quotas are determined on the proposal of International Programs Office, with the decree by the

preceding year. 
2. Quotas are determined on the proposal of International Programs Office, with the decree by the 
University Senate and by the approval of the Board of Trustees. TEDU is free whether or not fill up 
the quotas. If deemed necessary, quota transfer between programs are made possible. 
Application Requirements 
1. Candidates, whose application will be evaluated on the criteria of nationality and the nation where 
secondary education is completed are determined according to the “Principles on the Admission of 
Foreign Students” by the Council of Higher Education  
2. In this context, candidates, whose application is accepted, may be requested to document their 
financial capabilities to afford their higher education expenses in Turkey. 
Application Procedures 
1. Applications are available on the dates as declared on the Academic Calendar. 
2. The requested documents are completely submitted via online application interface. 
Evaluation Criteria

1. Applications are available on the dates as declared on the Academic Calendar. 
2. The requested documents are completely submitted via online application interface. 
Evaluation Criteria 
1. Exams which are accepted as equivalent of university entrance exams, diplomas and minimum 
scores required for the acceptance of applications are determined each year by the University Senate 
and submitted to the Council of Higher Education, and announced on the website thereon. 
2. Meeting application requirements does not guarantee admission to a program 
3. Students to be admitted to a previously announced quota may be from different nationalities. 
4. Unless stated otherwise, validity period of equivalent exams (SAT, etc.) is two years. There is no 
such limitation on high school graduation exams (GCE-AL, IB Diploma, Baccalaureate, etc) as well 
as high school graduation/diploma grades.

RULES AND PROCEDURES TO FOLLOW IN CASE OF VIOLATION OF 
ACADEMIC INTEGRITY 
Rules and procedures to follow in case of violation of academic honesty principles are regulated 
in line with continuing education, accountability and fair treatment principles of TED 
University. Taking into consideration that the university freshmen might be more likely to fall 
into error in this regard, particularly in terms of plagiarism, due to inexperience or lack of 
knowledge of the principles of academic integrity, a practice mechanism focusing on 
education/development has been provided for them. In this context, violations of academic 
integrity were classified under two categories, as first-degree and second-degree violations,

education/development has been provided for them. In this context, violations of academic 
integrity were classified under two categories, as first-degree and second-degree violations, 
based on its seriousness. Procedures to follow for either instance are given below: 
First-degree violations of academic integrity are considered as violations committed 
deliberately in a flagrant manner with the mere intention of fraud, cheating and deception. 
Examples include, but are not limited to, the following: 
 Submitting an assignment or a project, etc. prepared by another person as if it was 
his/her own work, 
 Having another person do his/her assignment/project in exchange of money or other 
benefits, 
 Doing another person’s assignment/project in exchange of money or other benefits, 
 Citing from another person’s work explicitly and carelessly in an assignment/project 
without giving necessary references (extensive plagiarism), 
 Attempting to cheat in exams,

 Citing from another person’s work explicitly and carelessly in an assignment/project 
without giving necessary references (extensive plagiarism), 
 Attempting to cheat in exams, 
 Cheating in exams, including those given as home assignments, 
 Having someone else sit his/her exam or sitting someone else’s exam, including those 
are held online, 
 Plagiarism in thesis writing, 
 Forging a document, 
 Fabricating data sets or inventing fictitious sources, 
 Taking unfair advantage. 
Second-degree violations of academic integrity are considered as violations committed 
unintentionally, inadvertently, due to academic inadequacy or sloppy writing habits. Examples 
include, but are not limited to, the following: 
 Partial citations lacking proper reference and covering a small percentage of the whole 
work, 
 Assignments/projects mostly consisting of citations, although properly referenced,

 Partial citations lacking proper reference and covering a small percentage of the whole 
work, 
 Assignments/projects mostly consisting of citations, although properly referenced, 
 Citing from an original source only by changing the linguistic or structural integrity, 
eliminating or replacing words or sentences.

Rules and Procedures to Follow in Case of Detection of First and Second Degree 
Violations: 
 An incident report is prepared by the course instructor or the proctor in case a first-
degree violation of academic honesty is detected and it is submitted to the related 
authority in charge in order to initiate a disciplinary proceeding. 
 In case a second-degree violation of academic integrity is detected by the course

authority in charge in order to initiate a disciplinary proceeding. 
 In case a second-degree violation of academic integrity is detected by the course 
instructor or the research assistant, one or more sanctions are applied respectively from 
mild to severe in proportion of the seriousness of the incident. If needed, it can be 
conferred with a member of Faculty Ethics Commission. 
Academic sanctions to be imposed in case a second-degree violation of academic honesty is 
detected are as follows: 
 Verbal warning: The course instructor summons the student and pronounces that he/she 
had committed an act of academic dishonesty and emphasizes the importance of 
observing these principles. 
 Reduction in assignment/project grade: The instructor reduces the grade of the 
assignment/project as deemed appropriate. 
 Resubmission of the assignment/project: The course instructor may require that the 
work in question be redone to conform to proper academic standards or may require that

 Resubmission of the assignment/project: The course instructor may require that the 
work in question be redone to conform to proper academic standards or may require that 
a new project be submitted. In this case, the instructor may still impose a sanction of 
grade reduction for the resubmitted assignment. 
 Grade reduction to “zero”: The grade of the assignment/project is reduced to “zero” or 
“F” excluding any right to compensation. 
In addition to these sanctions, related student may also be referred to the Center of Teaching 
and Learning in order to attend a course on “Academic Writing Practices.” In case the student 
does not agree to this sanction, the course instructor shall report it to the related disciplinary 
authority in charge. 
In case where a student commits a second-degree violation of academic integrity after having 
already been sanctioned for committing second-degree violations three times earlier, the course

In case where a student commits a second-degree violation of academic integrity after having

instructor shall report the situation to the related disciplinary authority in charge in order to 
determine which procedure to follow. 
Regulations to provide guidance to the faculties and departments can be made in order to ensure 
consistency of sanctions imposed against second-degree violations of academic integrity.
